The '''2025 Copa Libertadores final''' was the final match which decided the winner of the [[2025 Copa Libertadores]]. This was the 66th edition of the [[Copa Libertadores]], the top-tier South American continental club [[Association football|football]] tournament organized by [[CONMEBOL]].

The match was played by Brazilian clubs [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] and [[CR Flamengo|Flamengo]] on 29 November 2025 at the [[Estadio Monumental "U"|Estadio Monumental]] in [[Lima]], Peru, in a rematch of the [[2021 Copa Libertadores final|2021 final]].<ref name=Venue>{{cite web|url=https://www.infobae.com/deportes/2025/08/11/la-conmebol-confirmo-el-estadio-donde-se-jugara-la-final-de-la-libertadores-2025/ |title=La Conmebol confirmó el estadio donde se jugará la final de la Libertadores 2025 |trans-title=CONMEBOL confirmed the stadium where the 2025 Libertadores final will be played |publisher=[[Infobae]] |language=es |date=11 August 2025 |access-date=28 October 2025}}</ref>

Flamengo won their fourth Copa Libertadores title and became the first Brazilian team to win four titles in the competition by defeating Palmeiras 1–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgl640pzjjjt |title=Copa Libertadores final: Flamengo beat Palmeiras to win fourth title |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=29 November 2025 |access-date=29 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/47142896/danilo-header-lifts-flamengo-fourth-copa-libertadores-crown|title=Danilo's header lifts Flamengo to fourth Copa Libertadores crown|date=1 December 2025|work=ESPN|accessdate=1 December 2025}}</ref>
As winners of the 2025 Copa Libertadores, Flamengo qualified for the [[2025 FIFA Intercontinental Cup]] and the [[2029 FIFA Club World Cup]] and also earned the right to play against the winners of the [[2025 Copa Sudamericana]], [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]], in the [[2026 Recopa Sudamericana]]. They also automatically qualified for the [[2026 Copa Libertadores]] group stage.{{cn|date=December 2025}}

==Venue==
[[File:Estadio Monumental 2021.jpg|thumb|250x250px|The [[Estadio Monumental "U"|Estadio Monumental]] in [[Lima]] hosted the final.]]
On 28 April 2025, [[Lima]] was announced as the host city for the final match of the [[2025 Copa Libertadores]] at a stadium to be confirmed, following an application made by the [[Peruvian Football Federation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rpp.pe/futbol/copa-libertadores/final-de-copa-libertadores-lima-sera-sede-de-la-final-de-libertadores-2025-noticia-1631201 |title=¡Oficial! Lima será sede de la final de la Copa Libertadores 2025 |trans-title=Official! Lima will host the 2025 Copa Libertadores final |publisher=[[Radio Programas del Perú]] |language=es |date=28 April 2025 |access-date=28 October 2025}}</ref> The appointment was confirmed after a meeting between the president of [[CONMEBOL]] [[Alejandro Domínguez (football executive)|Alejandro Domínguez]] and the president of Peru [[Dina Boluarte]], who stated that the Peruvian government would commit to providing the necessary guarantees for the event to take place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/conmebol-libertadores/articles-video/conmebol-announced-lima-as-host-city-for-the-2025-copa-libertadores-final-2025-04-28|title=CONMEBOL announced Lima as host city for the 2025 Copa Libertadores Final|publisher=[[beIN Sports (American TV channel)|BeIN Sports]]|date=28 April 2025|access-date=15 May 2025}}</ref>

On 11 August 2025, CONMEBOL confirmed [[Estadio Monumental "U"|Estadio Monumental]] as the venue for the final match.<ref name=Venue/> This was the fourth Copa Libertadores final played in the Peruvian capital and the second held at Estadio Monumental after the [[2019 Copa Libertadores final|2019]] one, in which Brazilian club [[CR Flamengo|Flamengo]] defeated Argentine side [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.ar/futbol/copa-libertadores/nota/_/id/15112669/las-finales-de-conmebol-libertadores-que-se-disputaron-en-peru |title=Se viene la quinta: todas las finales de CONMEBOL Libertadores que se disputaron en Perú |trans-title=The fifth one is coming: all the CONMEBOL Libertadores finals that were played in Peru |publisher=[[ESPN (Latin America)|ESPN]] |language=es |date=4 October 2024 |access-date=28 October 2025}}</ref>

==Format==
The final was played as a single match at a pre-selected venue, with the higher-seeded team designated as the "home" team for administrative purposes. If scores were level after full time, 30 minutes of extra time would be played. If still tied after extra time, a penalty shoot-out would be used to determine the winner.<ref name="regulations">{{cite web|url=https://cdn.conmebol.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Manual-de-Clubes-CL-2025-ESP-Digital.pdf|title=Manual de Clubes CONMEBOL Libertadores 2025|trans-title=2025 CONMEBOL Libertadores Clubs Handbook|publisher=CONMEBOL|language=es|date=12 December 2024|access-date=16 December 2024}}</ref>

== Match ==
[[Weverton (footballer, born 1987)|Weverton]], [[Lucas Evangelista]] and [[Paulinho (footballer, born July 2000)|Paulinho]] (Palmeiras)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.antenadosnofutebol.com.br/libertadores/palmeiras-treina-sem-weverton-e-tem-tres-baixas-para-final-da-libertadores |title=Palmeiras treina sem Weverton e tem três baixas para final da Libertadores |publisher=Antenados no Futebol |language=pt |date=29 November 2025}}</ref> and [[Pedro (footballer, born 1997)|Pedro]] (Flamengo)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/2025/11/19/pedro-do-flamengo-tem-lesao-muscular-as-vesperas-da-final-da-libertadores-com-o-palmeiras.ghtml |title=Pedro, do Flamengo, sofre lesão muscular e está fora da final da Libertadores |publisher=Globo |language=pt |date=19 November 2025}}</ref> missed the final due to injuries, as well as [[Gonzalo Plata]] (Flamengo),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/2025/11/14/conmebol-pune-plata-com-dois-jogos-de-suspensao-e-multa-atacante-do-flamengo.ghtml |title=Conmebol pune Plata com dois jogos de suspensão e multa atacante do Flamengo |publisher=Globo |language=pt |date=14 November 2025}}</ref> who was ruled out due to suspension.

=== Summary===
In the 67th minute, Flamengo took the lead when [[Danilo (footballer, born July 1991)|Danilo]] scored the only goal of the game with a header to the left corner of the net after a corner from the right, took by [[Giorgian de Arrascaeta|Giorgian De Arascaeta]].
